blocks.text: Retrieval augmented fine-tuning, RAFT, trains a model specifically to use retrieved documents well, distinguishing relevant passages from irrelevant distractors and grounding its answers in the correct source material, rather than simply combining a generic fine-tuned model with retrieval augmented generation, covered in an earlier course, at inference time only.

This topic covers how RAFT training data deliberately includes distractor documents, why this produces a model that handles imperfect retrieval more gracefully, and how it connects to the broader RAG pipeline covered in an earlier course.
1. What RAFT Trains a Model to Do

blocks.alt: What RAFT Trains a Model to Do
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472912812-266099020.png

RAFT explicitly trains a model on examples that include retrieved context alongside the query, teaching it to answer specifically based on the provided documents rather than only relying on knowledge memorized during pretraining, connecting directly to the retrieval concepts covered in the earlier RAG and Vector Search course.
2. Standard RAG vs RAFT
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472912812-261940103.png

A standard RAG setup, covered in an earlier course, uses a general fine-tuned or base model and simply provides retrieved context at inference time, RAFT instead specifically trains the model during fine-tuning to handle retrieved context well, a distinction that matters because a model never trained on retrieval-augmented examples may not use provided context as effectively as one that was.
3. Training With Distractor Documents
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472912813-351627989.png

A key element of RAFT training data is deliberately including distractor documents, retrieved passages that are topically related but not actually relevant to answering the query, alongside the genuinely relevant document, teaching the model to distinguish useful context from noise rather than assuming everything retrieved is equally trustworthy.

code.content:
{"query": "What is the return policy for electronics?",
 "relevant_doc": "Electronics may be returned within 15 days with original packaging...",
 "distractor_doc": "Clothing items may be returned within 30 days...",
 "answer": "Electronics may be returned within 15 days with original packaging."}

blocks.text: 4. Why This Matters for Real Retrieval Quality

blocks.alt: Why This Matters for Real Retrieval Quality
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472913227-191249867.png

Real retrieval systems, covered in an earlier course, are never perfectly precise, some irrelevant documents inevitably get retrieved alongside relevant ones, a model trained with RAFT distractor documents learns to ground its answer in the genuinely relevant material even when noisy context is present, rather than being thrown off by it.

blocks.text: 5. Encouraging Traceable, Citation-Grounded Answers
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472913229-961883499.png

RAFT training data can additionally include reasoning steps that explicitly reference which retrieved passage supports the answer, encouraging the model to produce responses that are more traceable back to their source, directly addressing the hallucination concerns covered in the earlier Hallucination Evaluation topic.

blocks.title: This connects RAFT directly to the hallucination problem
blocks.content: A model trained to explicitly cite which retrieved passage grounds its answer is inherently working against the kind of unsupported claim generation that hallucination evaluation, covered in an earlier topic, is designed to catch.

blocks.text: 6. RAFT vs No Retrieval-Aware Training at All

blocks.alt: RAFT vs No Retrieval-Aware Training at All
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472913229-887590903.png

A model fine-tuned purely on standard instruction data, without any retrieval-augmented examples, has never explicitly practiced the specific skill of weighing provided context against its own internal knowledge, RAFT specifically closes this gap for use cases where retrieval augmented generation will be the deployment pattern.
7. Deploying a RAFT-Trained Model
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472913230-3085981.png

A RAFT-trained model is typically deployed as part of a full RAG pipeline, covered in the earlier RAG and Vector Search course, retrieval, re-ranking, and generation all still apply, RAFT specifically strengthens the generation stage ability to use whatever context that pipeline surfaces.
8. Building RAFT Training Data

Constructing RAFT training data requires both genuinely relevant documents and carefully chosen distractors for each query, the distractor selection process matters, distractors that are too obviously irrelevant teach the model little, distractors that are genuinely confusable with the relevant document teach a much sharper distinction.
9. When RAFT Is Worth the Investment

RAFT is particularly worth the additional training data effort for production RAG systems where retrieval precision is imperfect, which describes most real deployments, and where hallucination risk from misused retrieved context is a genuine concern for the application.
Worked Example

A team deploying a customer support RAG system finds their model sometimes blends information from an irrelevant retrieved document into its answer, producing subtly incorrect responses even when the correct document was also retrieved.

They build a RAFT training set specifically including distractor documents alongside relevant ones for each query, retraining their model to more reliably ground answers in the correct source, a follow up evaluation using the hallucination evaluation approach covered in an earlier topic confirms a measurable reduction in context-blending errors.
Common Mistakes

items: Training only on clean, single-relevant-document examples, never exposing the model to realistic retrieval noise
Choosing distractor documents that are too obviously irrelevant, teaching the model little useful discrimination
Treating RAFT as a replacement for good retrieval quality rather than a complement to it
Not evaluating specifically for context-grounding and hallucination reduction after a RAFT training pass

blocks.text: Practice

For a RAG based application you are familiar with or could imagine, sketch one RAFT training example including a query, a genuinely relevant document, and a plausible but incorrect distractor document, and write the answer your model should produce, grounded specifically in the relevant document.
Key Takeaway

Retrieval augmented fine-tuning explicitly trains a model on examples mixing relevant documents with distractors, teaching it to ground answers in genuinely relevant retrieved context rather than being confused by realistic retrieval noise, strengthening the generation stage of a full RAG pipeline covered in an earlier course and directly working against the hallucination risks covered in an earlier evaluation topic.
